newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's wise men see 2.5 pct 1997 growth.
newsitem.headline: Germany's wise men see 2.5 pct 1997 growth.

text.p: Germany's economy will grow 2.5 percent next year while unemployment remains high and inflation calm at about 1.75 percent, a government panel of five independent economic advisors said in an annual report.
The unemployment rate is likely to average about 11.7 percent, up from an average 11.4 percent this year, the panel said.

Germany's total public sector budget deficit will total 114 billion marks, or 3.3 percent of gross domestic product, exceeding the 3.0 percent guideline to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU), it said.
The panel said it could not exclude, however, the possibility that the three percent target could be met.
This is no reason to argue for a looser interpretation of the EMU criteria, it said.

A delay in the start of EMU would not spell the end of the project, it said. The European Commission's proposal for a stability pact covering adherence to the criteria after the start of EMU is not specific enough, it said.
German interest rates are likely to remain stable next year, and there is no need for a more restrictive monetary policy, the panel said.
